newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Parties insist Portugal set for euro in '99 - paper.
newsitem.headline: Parties insist Portugal set for euro in '99 - paper.

text.p: Portugal's two main parties are preparing a joint document to express their determination that Portugal will not be excluded from the first stage of Economic and Monetary Union (EMU), a newspaper said over the weekend.

Expresso weekly quoted sources in the ruling Socialist Party (PS) and opposition centre-right Social Democratic Party (PSD) as saying the joint document would be presented as a resolution at a parliamentary debate next Wednesday.
The resolution would undoubtedly pass as the two parties together account for the vast majority of seats in parliament.
PS and PSD officials were not immediately available to comment on the report.
The document would express Portugal's determination to join the European single currency, or euro, from the outset in January 1999, the newspaper reported.
It would also say that the choice of which countries join the euro from the start will be dictated by their ability to meet the targets set by the Maastricht Treaty.
It would express concern over comments by European officials recently raising doubts about the chances of Portugal and other Mediterranean states to join the euro in 1999.
The document will also highlight the progress that Portugal has made so far to meet the Maastricht criteria, Expresso said.
